entries.claim: An estimator is unbiased when its expectation equals the parameter; among unbiased estimators, smaller variance means greater efficiency
entries.notes: Sample mean cited as unbiased for the population mean

entries.claim: Standard error of the sample mean is sigma/sqrt(n), estimated by s/sqrt(n) when sigma is unknown
entries.notes: Assumes independent observations; s uses denominator n-1

entries.claim: When sigma is unknown the population-mean confidence interval is x-bar plus or minus t_(1-alpha/2, n-1) times s/sqrt(n)
entries.notes: Student-t critical value with n-1 degrees of freedom

entries.claim: Two-sided normal critical values are 1.645 (90%), 1.960 (95%) and 2.576 (99%)
entries.notes: Values used only in the large-sample teaching approximation

entries.claim: The confidence level is the long-run coverage frequency of the procedure, not the probability that a fixed parameter lies in one computed interval
entries.notes: Frequentist interpretation; Bayesian credible intervals are a different object

entries.claim: Method of moments matches sample and population moments; maximum likelihood maximizes the likelihood of the observed data, and neither is universally unbiased
entries.notes: Normal-variance MLE uses denominator n and is biased

entries.claim: With x-bar=173.0, s=6.8, n=30 the 95% t interval is about [170.5, 175.5]
Among 20 illustrative 95% intervals, 19 cover mu and 1 misses
entries.notes: Hand-placed segments; only the 95% coverage idea is claimed, not exact widths
